messages.content: I'm planning a trip to Munich and need to check the weather for this Sunday. Can you retrieve the weather forecast for Munich?

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

message.reasoning:
The user wants the weather forecast for Munich for this Sunday. We need to use the Open-Meteo API. The function signature is requests_get. We need to provide URL, headers, timeout, params, etc. The URL for Open-Meteo API: "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast". We need to set latitude and longitude for Munich. Munich coordinates: approx 48.1351° N, 11.5820° E. So latitude=48.1351, longitude=11.5820. We want forecast for this Sunday. We need to specify the forecast parameters. The Open-Meteo API supports daily parameters like temperature_2m_max, temperature_2m_min, precipitation_sum, etc. We need to specify the timezone. We can set timezone=Europe/Berlin. We need to specify start_date and end_date. We need to compute the date for this Sunday. Today is 2026-05-31. Let's find the next Sunday. 2026-05-31 is a Thursday. The next Sunday is 2026-06-04. So we need start_date=2026-06-04, end_date=2026-06-04. We need to specify daily=temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,precipitation_sum,weathercode. Also we need to set "forecast_days" maybe. But we can just set start_date and end_date. The API expects "start_date" and "end_date" as query parameters. So we need to include them in params. Also we need to include "daily" param. The "daily" param expects a comma-separated list of daily variables. So we can set daily="temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,precipitation_sum,weathercode". Also we need to set "timezone" param. So we need to include timezone=Europe/Berlin. So the params object will include:

{
  latitude: 48.1351,
  longitude: 11.5820,
  daily: "temperature_2m_max,temperature_2m_min,precipitation_sum,weathercode",
  timezone: "Europe/Berlin",
  start_date: "2026-06-04",
  end_date: "2026-06-04"
}

We also need to set headers. The default headers are {"Content-Type":"application/json","Accept":"application/json"}. We can leave them as default. We can set timeout=10.0. We can leave other optional fields as default.

Thus we call the function requests_get with the arguments.
